Are you out of your pixel? — the local instrument

A local instrument that measures one thing: did an AI action stay inside the lane it was authorized to operate in? It weighs what was authorized (Intent) against what actually happened (Reality) and the outcome you ruled out (Negative), and returns a sealed IN_LANE / OFF_DOMAIN / UNPLACEABLE verdict — no cloud, and no model anywhere in the measurement; nothing leaves this machine. The panels below are that measurement running live on-chip — the same walk the commit emails ship.
The concession, before any claim: WHERE an action landed is decidable — provable, re-runnable, no model in the verdict. WHETHER the work is good is undecidable (Rice) — this instrument never claims that, and never will. Every number on this page carries the command that recomputes it; you are not asked to trust anything you cannot re-run.
🔒
ZERO-LLM VERIFICATION · 100% LOCAL PMU · ZERO CLOUD EXFILTRATION The panels are the running pipeline (runPipeline → renderTriptych, the real recursive walk). The interactive what-ifs re-run that SAME on-chip walk through the local /render endpoint (127.0.0.1) — the browser holds no compression engine of its own; the display is a pure projection of the metal. No fetch to the internet, no external asset, no model in the measurement path. The terminal's LLM is an adversary trying to break the math, never in it.

The Greeks — priced off the drift series, not the price series

—
Δ delta — weighted Semantic Bleed σ
—
Δ-spread — max Chebyshev king-move leak
—
Γ gamma — traction slope (drift rate-of-change)
—
𝒱 vega — reef volatility (hold-rate variance)
—
Θ theta — efficiency decay vs Lens-OFF base

Everything above this line is a measurement. These five are the Greeks. An option desk takes the volatility of a price series; there is no second construction that takes it of a semantic one — that is what 𝒱 vega is here, and it is the reason a drift series can be underwritten at all. Each value is read from the newest ed25519-signed lens signal, never recomputed for display and never produced by a model — npx thetacog-mcp attest re-derives the same numbers offline. A dash is an honest absence with its reason in the tooltip (hover it): a Greek whose source has no data stays null rather than becoming a plausible number, which is the only version of this instrument an underwriter can price. Dashes on a fresh install are correct — no reference numbers are shipped, because these Greeks are supposed to be measured on your repository. Run npx thetacog-install-hooks and commit once: the post-commit hook emits your first signed signal and this row fills with your own.

The tesseract is not a grid — it is the descent computed for one prompt. The lattice has 144 ShortLex anchors per axis, so a depth-0 state is 144² = 20,736 cells. But a cell subdivides under semantic pressure: when enough mass accumulates at one coordinate it materializes its own 144-cell sub-well, and the addressable space becomes 144d+1 at descent depth d — depth 1 alone is 2,985,984 positions, 144× the cloud drawn here. What the panels render is the 12 × 12 shadow of that structure at depth 0. Honest state today: 1 of 144 sub-wells is materialized (E1 returned NO-GO at contrast C=0.825 — cells failed by incoherence within, not blobbiness between), so we live at depth 0 and the realized space is 20,880 positions — 0.699% of the depth-1 potential. Depth is the open frontier, not a shipped claim.

Actuarial signals — what this instrument already counts (you price which ones)

  

    
You don't have to design the telemetry. Every measurement above emits countable, timestamped, recomputable signals — the raw material of a rate. Here are the ones an underwriter typically wants; tell us which you'd price, and the policy keys on them. (The monologue we're after: "I can't underwrite a heat-map, but I can underwrite that Boolean — and here are the counts that build the rate.")

    

      
SignalWhat it countsWhat an actuary does with it

      
OFF_DOMAIN ratebreaches per N actions (Mode A + Mode B)the base claim frequency — the headline rate.

      
Mode A vs Mode B mixdrift breaches vs catastrophe breachestwo severity tiers priced separately — gradual drift ≠ domain-shift catastrophe.

      
Margin to the excluded domaindN − dI (how close to the third rail)a leading indicator — tightening margin predicts a Mode B before it fires.

      
Abstention rateUNPLACEABLE events (ties the instrument refused)a data-quality / spec-looseness signal — high abstention means the lane needs sharpening.

      
Time-in-lane %the complement of off-lane over a bookthe good-behavior credit — the basis for an experience discount.

      
Drift velocityhow fast drift% climbs across a sessiona trend/renewal signal — a book drifting upward reprices at renewal.

    

    
Every one is a discrete, recomputable event — not a model's opinion. That is the precondition for pricing a book rather than inspecting a single incident.

  


  
  
What we built · what we did NOT build · what's next

  

    
What we built. A localized, deterministic liability trigger that measures the structural distance between authorized intent, realized action, and the excluded domain — with no LLM inference in the measurement path and nothing leaving the machine.

    
What we did NOT build — and the objection each omission kills:

    
No continuous onChange recompute. You press a button; the instrument takes a discrete measurement and seals it. Prevented: "it's a jittery calculator guessing as I type — subjective." Enforced: "it takes a measurement, seals it, stamps a finalized receipt — a discrete, countable event."

    
No single-word ("left vs right kidney") examples. The presets are structural negation — Drafting vs Executing, a shift in operational authority. Prevented: "if it just matches the word 'left,' a cheaper keyword filter does this." Enforced: "it caught a breach of authority a keyword filter would miss."

    
No LLM in the verification path. The on-chip definer-walk does the measurement (via the local /render endpoint, 127.0.0.1); the terminal's model is the adversary, not the judge. Prevented: "he's asking an AI to grade another AI — a black box in a black box." Enforced: "the measurement is pure arithmetic; the model is excluded from the receipt."

    
No cloud sync. Sensitive AI-incident logs never leave the deployer's machine. Prevented: "I can't upload client incident logs to a third-party startup server." Enforced: "the instrument is air-gapped; the record is yours."

    
What's next — the bare-metal standard. This page drives the real on-chip definer-walk through the local /render endpoint (127.0.0.1) — the browser holds no measurement engine of its own. The legally-binding production standard is the bare-metal Linux definer-walk — the same measurement, hardware-deterministic, built for massive parallel verification. The local walk you see here and the Linux walk agree by construction; the receipt is portable across both.

BATTERY SATURATED — this panel cannot answer its own question yet. The ungrounded baseline already routes 22/22, so every grounding level reads identical BY CONSTRUCTION. What grounding COSTS is measured (separation falls monotonically with cap). What it BUYS is not measured, and no number here should be read as an optimum.
Limit: n=22 labeled prompts. One prompt = 4.5pp, so only multi-prompt gaps mean anything. Measures ROUTING accuracy only — not answer quality, not enrichment usefulness. A saturated baseline makes every row uninformative regardless of n.
What would measure it: a battery of prompts the ungrounded lens gets WRONG — deictic fragments (the 18 no-lane prompts already catalogued in unenriched-report.json are exactly this population), or prompts whose ideal domain is a near-neighbour of where they place ungrounded. Until such a battery exists, the grounding cap is an un-derivable judgment and must stay labelled as one.
